title: Early Lactate-Guided Sepsis Resuscitation in Emergency Care
subtitle: Synthetic Teaching Summary of Burden, Endothelial Pathophysiology, and Hour-1 Bundle Protocol

epidemiology_kpis.label: Global annual sepsis cases (synthetic teaching ref)
Relative mortality rise per hour antimicrobial delay

mechanism_steps.detail: Pathogen recognition triggers TLR4/NF-kB innate cytokine surge (IL-1b, TNF-a, IL-6).
Endothelial barrier breakdown causes capillary leak, nitric oxide vasoplegia, and microthrombi.
Impaired microvascular O2 extraction shifts pyruvate toward lactate >= 2.0 mmol/L.
SOFA rise >= 2 points across renal, pulmonary, hepatic, and circulatory systems.

clinical_pathway.criteria: qSOFA / NEWS2 trigger; draw 2 sets blood cultures + venous/arterial lactate prior to antimicrobials.
Administer IV antimicrobials tailored to suspected focus and local resistance antibiogram.
Infuse 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid for hypotension (MAP < 65 mmHg) or lactate >= 4.0 mmol/L.
Initiate norepinephrine to target MAP >= 65 mmHg; repeat serum lactate at 2 hours (target >= 20% clearance).

education_pearls: Normal blood pressure does NOT exclude cryptic septic shock when serum lactate is >= 4.0 mmol/L.
Never delay empiric IV antimicrobials > 45 minutes while awaiting imaging or lumbar puncture.
Prefer balanced crystalloids (lactated Ringer's / Plasma-Lyte) over high-chloride 0.9% saline to reduce AKI risk.
Reassess dynamic fluid responsiveness (capillary refill, passive leg raise) before additional boluses.
